title: Finite normalization of the system projection-evaluation word
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$, $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every scheme $W$ use a small skeleton of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, completed coefficient sheaf $R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$, and ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. On the vertical sequence site write $\mathcal Q_W(n,U)=(A_n)_W(U)$, $R_W^{\mathrm{const}}$ for the constant sequence ring, $\mathscr P$ for the one-point sequence topos, and $\mathcal A=(A_n)_n$ for its quotient ring [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Let $\rho_W:(W^{\mathrm{Tow}},\mathcal Q_W)\to(W^{\mathrm{Tow}},R_W^{\mathrm{const}})$ and $\rho_0:(\mathscr P,\mathcal A)\to(\mathscr P,R)$ be scalar restriction morphisms. Write $g_W^{\mathcal Q}$ and $g_W^R$ for point-sections morphisms to these one-point sequence topoi, with $g_W^R\rho_W=\rho_0g_W^{\mathcal Q}$. The symbol $Rg_*$ means derived sections with values in towers, without inverse limit. Restriction $\rho_*$ is exact. Use the derived internal Hom and signed closed tensor-Hom structure [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model].
Let $k$ be a field with $\ell$ invertible, and let $a:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes, with a fixed compactification $X\xrightarrow j Z\xrightarrow pY$, $pj=a$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the quotient sequence sites put $F^{\mathcal Q}=Rp_*^{\mathcal Q}j_!$, with proper image derived after exact open extension, and $F_n=Rp_{*,n}j_!$ at $A_n$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. For $K\in D(R_X)$ put $V=\operatorname{const}K$ and $M=L\rho_X^*V$, with $M_n=K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$ and actual quotient transitions [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction].
Let $N\in D(\mathcal Q_X)$, $N_n=\operatorname{ev}_nN$, $D=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal Q_X}(M,N)$, $h=Rg_{X*}^{\mathcal Q}D$, $b_M=Rg_{Y*}^{\mathcal Q}F^{\mathcal Q}M$, and $b_N=Rg_{Y*}^{\mathcal Q}F^{\mathcal Q}N$. Specify $\widetilde\beta_{M,N}$ by the sequence-site word of [lem-coef-system-projection-evaluation]: scalar balancing, symmetry, the sections projection mate, the proper projection mate, open tensor comparison and closed evaluation after the $g_X$ counit. Use the Hom tower and its canonical comparison of [lem-coef-hom-tower-scalar-model], and the support comparisons of [lem-coef-support-open-tensor-model]. Let $B_K=\rho_{0*}b_M$ and $B_N=\rho_{0*}b_N$, and let $\beta_{K,N}:\mathsf H_N(K)\otimes_R^LB_K\to B_N$ be its transport by the full-system scalar-Hom comparison. Then, under the canonical exact evaluation/tensor isomorphism and the comparisons
$$\operatorname{ev}_n\mathsf H_N(K)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_{X,A_n}(K_n,N_n),\quad\operatorname{ev}_nB_K\cong R\Gamma(Y,F_nK_n),\quad\operatorname{ev}_nB_N\cong R\Gamma(Y,F_nN_n),$$
the map $\operatorname{ev}_n\beta_{K,N}$ is exactly
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{X,A_n}(K_n,N_n)\otimes_R^LR\Gamma(Y,F_nK_n)\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_{X,A_n}(K_n,N_n)\otimes_{A_n}^LR\Gamma(Y,F_nK_n)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(Y,F_nN_n).$$
The first arrow is scalar balancing. In the second, the finite sections mate is followed by the ambient compact-support projection of [def-exchange-projection] with the actual open tensor comparison, and then finite evaluation after the sections counit. More precisely the evaluated adjoint defining $\pi_p$ is $(\varepsilon_{p,j_!K_n}\otimes1)\mu_p$, the evaluated $g_X$ counit is the ordinary finite sections counit, and the evaluated $\gamma$ is the sheafified open chain map. Direct-image composition comparisons, scalar restriction and pullback-composition comparisons carry these specified words and their units and counits to the finite ones. These identities apply to the already constructed system morphism; they require no K-injectivity of evaluations on the varying-ring site and no lifting or uniqueness principle for compatible finite derived maps. For $Y=\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ the point-sections convention is [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point].

proof.text: Use the ordinary derived system calculus of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] on the small vertical sequence sites. The coefficient maps are the actual quotient maps, so no flatness assumption is needed. The object $M=L\rho_X^*\operatorname{const}K$ is cartesian: under the scalar-extension composition and reduction cocycle of [lem-coef-semilinear-system-existence], its reduction adjunct is the associativity identification $(K\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_m)_X)\otimes^L_{(A_m)_X}(A_n)_X\cong K\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$. Thus the cartesian-first-input Hom evaluation theorem applies to $D=R\mathcal Hom(M,N)$, although $N$ is arbitrary. Exact evaluation gives $D_n\cong R\mathcal Hom_{(A_n)_X}(K_n,N_n)$ and carries its evaluation morphism to the finite one. Derived point sections then give $h_n\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_{X,A_n}(K_n,N_n)$ by the same geometric evaluation comparison.

proof.text: For $f=p$ and for the point-sections morphisms $g_X,g_Y$, apply the unit/counit and transpose compatibilities in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. With the canonical tensor and pull/push comparisons understood, evaluation sends $Rf_*(t)\eta_f$, the transpose of any $t:Lf^*C\to E$, to $Rf_{*,n}(t_n)\eta_{f,n}$. Taking $t=(\varepsilon_{f,E}\otimes1)\mu_f$ therefore gives the finite projection mate; in particular $e_n\pi_{p;j_!M,L}=\pi_{p,n;j_!K_n,L_n}$ and its defining adjoint is exactly $(\varepsilon_{p,j_!K_n}\otimes1)\mu_p$. The same formula for $g_Y$ gives the finite sections projection mate, and for $g_X$ it identifies the sections counit. These are identities of the specified maps, rather than just isomorphisms of their sources and targets.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint) and 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); agent specialization to the sequence-site word of blueprint prop-coef-integral-dualizing, proof paragraph 2.

proof.text: Evaluate the actual open tensor comparison using [lem-coef-support-open-tensor-model]. Its chain component is the sheafification of $u\otimes l\mapsto u\otimes l|_X$, so its evaluation is the same map over $(A_n)_Z$. The pullback-composition comparison and $g_X=g_Ya$ identify $La_n^*Lg_{Y,n}^*h_n$ with $Lg_{X,n}^*h_n$; the composition and transpose compatibilities of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] preserve this identification and its counit. Consequently the evaluated map $v_{M,N}$ in [lem-coef-system-projection-evaluation] is $K_n\otimes^L La_n^*Lg_{Y,n}^*h_n\to K_n\otimes^L D_n\to N_n$, with the first arrow induced by the finite sections counit and the second by the recorded symmetry followed by finite closed evaluation. The signed symmetry is unchanged under exact tensor evaluation.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-semilinear-operations-existence] to the map of ring towers $R^{\mathrm{const}}\to\mathcal A$ on the singleton site. This supplies the ScalarSystems comparison of [def-coef-semilinear-derived-calculus], normalized by scalar-adjunction transpose. Hence evaluation identifies $L\rho_0^*\dashv\rho_{0*}$, including unit and counit, with $A_n\otimes_R^L-\dashv\operatorname{Res}_n$. Evaluating the defining scalar word $c_{H,B}=\rho_{0*}(1\otimes\varepsilon_{\rho_0,B})\pi_{\rho_0}$ of [lem-coef-system-projection-evaluation] therefore gives
$$\operatorname{Res}_nH_n\otimes_R^L\operatorname{Res}_nB_n\xrightarrow{\pi_{r_n}}\operatorname{Res}_n(H_n\otimes_{A_n}^L Lr_n^*\operatorname{Res}_nB_n)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Res}_n(1\otimes\varepsilon_{r_n,B_n})}\operatorname{Res}_n(H_n\otimes_{A_n}^LB_n),$$
where $r_n$ is the scalar morphism for $R\to A_n$. This is the canonical scalar-balancing map: its scalar-adjunction transpose is the tensor of the two extension-restriction counits after the strong tensor comparison. This last description follows by substituting $\pi_{r_n}=Rr_{n*}((\varepsilon\otimes1)\mu)\eta$ and the triangle identity. No preservation of K-injectives by varying-ring evaluation is used.

proof.text: Specialize [lem-coef-system-projection-evaluation] at $U=M$. Its final clause fixes $\mathsf H_N(K)$ and its Hom comparison to be those of [lem-coef-hom-tower-scalar-model]. Use that theorem with $W=X$: its representative $I$ is resolved in constant-$R_X$ towers, and its finite input $K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$ is exactly this item's input. Substitute steps 1–4 in the specified word $\widetilde\beta_{M,N}=\rho_{0*}(q_{M,N}\circ\sigma_{h,b_M})\circ c_{h,b_M}$ of [lem-coef-system-projection-evaluation]. Functoriality of evaluation preserves the order of composition. Its first arrow is the scalar balancing of step 4. After it, the symmetry puts $b_{M,n}$ before $h_n$; the sections projection mate gives derived sections of $F_nK_n\otimes^LLg_{Y,n}^*h_n$; the proper projection mate followed by the evaluated open comparison gives derived sections of $F_n(K_n\otimes^LLa_n^*Lg_{Y,n}^*h_n)$; finally step 3 gives derived sections of $F_nN_n$. By the defining word of [def-exchange-projection], the proper/open portion is $\operatorname{PF}^c_{a,K_n,Lg_{Y,n}^*h_n}=Rp_{*,n}(\gamma)\circ\pi_{p;j_!K_n,Lg_{Y,n}^*h_n}$, the ambient compact-support projection, with the same symmetry convention: its $\pi_p$ is the evaluated mate of step 2, and its open factor is the open-immersion projection map named in that definition, followed by $Lj^*Lp^*\cong La^*$. By [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], for the constant finite ring $A_n$ its canonical $\gamma$ is precisely that named open-immersion projection map, and by [lem-coef-support-open-tensor-model] this canonical $\gamma$ is the evaluation of the system open comparison used in step 3. Thus this composite is precisely the second arrow asserted in the statement, preceded by scalar balancing.

proof.text: For the Hom comparison fixed in step 5, use [lem-coef-hom-tower-scalar-model]: its full-system isomorphism $\mathsf H_N(K)\cong\rho_{0*}h$ has finite comparison for derived scalar extension along $R_X\to(A_n)_X$, normalized by the actual reduction unit; its scalar internal-Hom comparison carries evaluation, after the scalar-extension unit, to restricted quotient-linear evaluation. Thus transporting $\widetilde\beta$ along it does not insert a further automorphism into the finite word just computed. The compact-support comparison of [lem-coef-support-open-tensor-model] identifies $e_nB_K$ with $R\Gamma(Y,F_nK_n)$, including direct-image composition and scalar restriction. For $B_N$ the same equality $e_nRg_{Y*}^{\mathcal Q}Rp_*^{\mathcal Q}j_!N\cong R\Gamma(Y,Rp_{*,n}j_!N_n)$ follows from geometric evaluation in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], which applies to arbitrary $N$. These comparisons carry all units, counits and pullback compositions used in steps 2–5 to the finite ones. The required equality for $e_n\beta_{K,N}$ follows. It was obtained by evaluating an already specified system composite; no reconstruction from compatible finite maps occurs.
